Saadia-specific moves preserved per data-source/saadia-gloss-table.json; Blau's notes (data-source/blau-genesis-notes.json) consulted. translations.1: The heavens and the earth and all their hosts were completed.
translations.2: And God completed on the seventh day His creation that He had made; and He desisted on it from creating anything from the like of His creation that He had made.
translations.3: And God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, since He desisted on it from creating anything from the like of His creation that He had made.
translations.4: This is the exposition of the origins of the sky and the earth, when they were created — at the time God made the earth and the sky.
translations.5: And all the trees of the wilderness, before they were upon the earth, and all its herbage, before it grew — since God had not rained upon it, nor was there a human to till it,
translations.6: nor was a vapor rising up from it to water all its face —
translations.7: And God created Adam — dust from the earth — and breathed into his nostril the breath of life; and Adam became a rational soul.
translations.8: And God planted a garden in Eden, easterly, and placed there the Adam whom He had created.
translations.9: And God caused to grow from the earth every tree fair of appearance and good for eating; and the tree of life in the midst of the garden; and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
translations.10: And there was a river going out from Eden to water the garden; and from there it divided, and became four heads.
translations.11: The name of one of them is the Nile (Pishon); and it is the one encompassing all the land of Zawila (Havilah), where the gold is.
translations.12: And the gold of that land is good; there are the pearls and the crystal stones.
translations.13: And the name of the second river is Gihon; it is the one encompassing all the land of Abyssinia (Cush).
translations.14: And the name of the third river is the Tigris (Hiddekel); it is the one running east of Mosul (Asshur). And the fourth river is the Euphrates.
translations.15: Then God took Adam, and settled him in the garden of Eden, to till it and to guard it.
translations.16: And God commanded him, saying: 'From every tree of the garden it is permitted that you eat;
translations.17: but from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil you shall not eat — for on the day you eat from it, you shall deserve to die.'
translations.18: Then God said: 'There is no good in Adam's remaining alone; I shall make for him a helper facing him.'
translations.19: And God gathered from the earth all the wild creatures of the wilderness and the bird of the sky, and brought them to Adam, to show him what he would name them. And every living soul that Adam named — that is its name to this day.
translations.20: And when Adam had named names for all the beasts and the bird of the sky and the wild creatures of the wilderness — he did not find for himself a helper facing him.
translations.21: And God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, so that he should not feel it, and he slept; and He extracted one of his ribs, and closed up its place with flesh.
translations.22: And He built from it a woman, and brought her to Adam.
translations.23: And Adam said: 'This time I have seen bone from my bones and flesh from my flesh — it is fitting that she be called Woman, because from Man she was taken.'
translations.24: Therefore a man leaves his father and his mother and cleaves to his wife; and the two become a single body.
translations.25: And the two of them together were naked — Adam and his wife — and they did not feel shame at it.
